clue.text: No restoration for me after collapse

definitions.text: No restoration for me after collapse

parts.words: No restoration for me after collapse
parts.note: the speaker is the egg of the nursery rhyme who had a great fall and could not be put together again by the king's horses and men

explanation.surface: A ruined thing laments that nobody will ever rebuild it.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery-rhyme egg falls off a wall, and 'all the king's horses and all the king's men' cannot reassemble him.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme ends with the egg character broken beyond any repair, so he speaks the line himself.

clue.text: Thought Welsh got in old dance in secluded spot

indicators.note: the thought and Welsh pieces are placed inside the old dance word, which takes them in

parts.note: the hay (or hey) is an old country dance
a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: A Welsh idea is slipped into an old folk dance in some remote corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' signals the container. The hay, or hey, is an old English country dance in which dancers weave in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat or hiding place is a secluded spot where one can be away from others.

clue.text: Short note on uplifting student song for a record

parts.note: a memo is a short note, itself a shortened memorandum

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the following pieces are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for student
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A brief note about a student song earmarked for recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses student plus song, and in a down clue 'on' means that piece sits below the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument or written commemoration is a lasting record of a person or event.

clue.text: Display mark on skin

definitions.meaning: a military display, such as the Edinburgh show of marching bands
a permanent inked design pricked into the skin

explanation.surface: Showing off a mark on one's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both an evening military pageant and an inked skin design, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Comic piper is among dramatist trivia

indicators.note: the reworked piper letters sit among those of the dramatist, inside his name

parts.note: Christopher Fry was an English verse dramatist

indicators.note: comic suggests the word piper is played around with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A funny pipe player turns up among a playwright's odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' rearranges the piper, and 'is among' splits the dramatist's surname around it. 'Dramatist' could be many names; the three-letter Fry fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills and trifles, showy things of no importance, are trivia.

clue.text: Offensive position

definitions.meaning: a grade or standing in a hierarchy, as in the army

explanation.surface: An attacking post, in military terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both foul-smelling and a level of standing such as an officer's grade.

clue.text: Eg stripe worn for high status?

indicators.note: something worn out or worn into a new shape has its letters rearranged here

explanation.surface: Is a stripe on the uniform worn as a mark of rank?
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' rearranges the letters of EG STRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown and standing in others' eyes are what high status amounts to.

clue.text: Good to see, say, one settling at the storm centre

definitions.text: say, one settling at the storm centre
definitions.meaning: someone resting lightly upon the calm middle of a hurricane, read literally

explanation.surface: Something pleasant to watch, like a person settling down at the heart of a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a hurricane's calm centre is its eye, and one settled there is resting easily on it; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pleasant to look at, and literally describes someone resting calmly in a hurricane's centre.

clue.text: A bit of yellow layer, possibly, occurring from time to time

indicators.note: only a small bit of yellow, its opening letter, is taken
possibly signals that the word layer may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A trace of a yellow stratum, perhaps, turning up now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' takes Y from yellow; 'possibly' turns LAYER into EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual happens once every twelve months, recurring at intervals.

clue.text: See 1 across
Dues near, perhaps, as subs could be

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of dues near may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Subscription dues come close, as membership subs might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subs' looks like subscriptions beside 'Dues', but it means submarines. 'perhaps' rearranges DUES NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarines travel beneath the waves, so they operate below the sea's surface.

clue.text: Ways to the town centre? Make them for progress

definitions.meaning: roads leading into a town, read literally as the answer
to advance against resistance, one is said to make these

explanation.surface: Routes into town: build them and things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word into IN ROADS, routes going in; the second is the idiom 'make inroads', meaning to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Routes heading into town, and the advances one makes in the idiom of progressing against opposition.

clue.text: Composer captures brio excitingly above a certain level

indicators.note: the composer's name surrounds and holds the reworked brio letters

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia

indicators.note: excitingly suggests the letters of brio are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A composer's music has a lively verve that soars to great heights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitingly' rearranges brio, and 'captures' sets it within the composer's name, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying or carried in the air means being up above the ground.

clue.text: The way to swagger, saunter

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way
to roll is to walk with a swaggering gait

explanation.surface: Advice on how to walk with swagger: just saunter.
explanation.walkthrough: ST (street, a way) plus ROLL, a swaggering walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk, an amble, is a saunter.

clue.text: Boron left beneath a fault

parts.note: B is the chemical symbol for boron
under is a synonym of beneath

explanation.surface: A chemist leaves boron lying underneath, by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' looks like a placement instruction, but here it supplies UNDER itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy mistake is a fault or error.

clue.text: A beer? It's just open!

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: Someone offered a beer says it has only just been cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'a jar' is a drink of beer at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A door slightly open, not quite shut, is just open.

clue.text: Educational course?

parts.note: reads as a programme of study, but course is a stage of a meal, here a steamed dessert named after an academic institution

explanation.surface: A course of study at a place of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a dish in a meal, not a programme of study: this is an old British steamed suet pudding with dried fruit, named after Cambridge colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamed suet dessert served as the sweet course of a meal, named for the academic halls where it was served.

clue.text: Delay in match — body seen in flight

indicators.note: the delay word is placed inside the match word

parts.note: a fusee is a large-headed match that will light in wind
a lag is a delay or time gap

explanation.surface: A hold-up in a sporting match, and a body is spotted in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' reads as a game, but it is a fusee, a windproof match; 'in' sets the delay inside it before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of an aircraft, which carries crew and passengers in flight.

clue.text: Fed up and finished, but acted as lawyer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: ended means finished

explanation.surface: Fed up and done for, yet he still argued in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF, followed by ENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister who argued a client's case in court spoke on their behalf as counsel.

clue.text: Declare the punishment in a number of words

definitions.meaning: what a judge does when announcing the penalty for a crime
a grammatical unit made of several words

explanation.surface: A judge passes judgement in carefully chosen words.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means a judge pronouncing a penalty; the noun is a grammatical string of words.

clue.text: See 16
We hear the top player's to give up

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament such as tennis

explanation.surface: Rumour says the champion is about to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: A seed is a ranked top player in a tennis draw; the word sounds like CEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or surrender something, such as territory, is to give it up.

clue.text: See 7
A dog: an animal in a wager

indicators.note: the animal is placed inside the wager word

parts.note: a bet is a wager
an ass is a donkey, an animal

explanation.surface: A dog, an animal: someone has placed a bet on one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the animal inside the wager, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged hound with long ears is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Redecorate V and A for universal approval

indicators.note: redecorate suggests giving the letters V, A and for, with the added piece, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: The V and A museum is redecorated, and everyone approves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redecorate' rearranges V, A, FOR and U (universal). The V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill and liking shown towards someone is approval.

clue.text: Supreme contentment welcome in a farmyard favourite

indicators.note: the welcome word is set inside the farmyard bird

parts.note: a hen is a familiar farmyard bird
ave is a Latin greeting of welcome

explanation.surface: A welcome sight in the farmyard brings perfect bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets the Latin greeting inside the farmyard bird, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect bliss, the supreme contentment.

clue.text: Several years with books declining?

parts.note: a decade is a span of ten years
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Years spent with books, yet in decline?
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in moral or cultural decline is declining.

clue.text: Half separate layer in the back

indicators.note: only half of the word for separate, its opening four letters, is used

parts.note: discrete means separate or distinct

explanation.surface: Half of a separate layer is in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Discrete means separate; 'Half' keeps its first four letters, DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartilage pads between the vertebrae of the spine are layers in the back.

clue.text: One on cloud 9 is, as one in 25 is?

definitions.text: One on cloud 9 is, as one in 25 is?

parts.words: One on cloud 9 is, as one in 25 is?
parts.note: describes the emotional state of someone on cloud nine, or of someone in the place of supreme contentment at 25 across

explanation.surface: Someone on cloud nine feels the way the blessed in paradise do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On cloud nine' is an idiom for being overjoyed; 25 across is a place of perfect bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Overjoyed or enraptured is how anyone in a state of bliss feels.

clue.text: Capital game that links two City banks

parts.note: the capital of the UK
a card game for four players in partnerships

explanation.surface: A city-based game that connects two banks in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City banks' suggests finance, but these are the riverbanks of the Thames: the crossing joins the City of London to Southwark.
explanation.definitionFit: A river crossing joins two shores, and this one spans the Thames at the City.

clue.text: Establish northern church after short course

indicators.note: the course comes first, with the northern church pieces placed after it
short means the course word loses its final letter

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Northern church established after a brief course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter off the meal course, an entrée, and 'after' places it before the northern church pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in or fix firmly so as to be hard to remove is to establish.

clue.text: See 29 across
